description.text: Get a bounded range of the markdown notes, the complete derived markdown summary, the complete attendee list without email addresses, and (when requested and available) a bounded range of the recorded transcript of a specific meeting. Use after search_meetings to answer anything about what was discussed, decided, the action items, or who-said-what. Returns start/end times for when the meeting happened. The raw Lexical notes JSON is intentionally omitted; use `content` for the paginated markdown note body and `summary` for the Flow Summary body, whose next-steps section holds the meeting's action items. Prefer view_transcript={} and synthesize your answer from the transcript itself: the notes are an auto-generated summary that can drop details, while the transcript is the verbatim source of truth. Omit view_transcript only when you've judged the notes alone are enough (e.g. a quick high-level recap). Transcript responses are character-bounded; when truncated, use the continuation offset in the marker to request the next range. Content is also character-bounded and returns its first range by default; use view_content with the continuation offset to read more. The summary is always returned in full. Available meetings include the user's own meetings, meetings shared with them as an email recipient, and meetings in enabled shared folders they can access. Shared meetings expose the summary and any transcript permitted by sharing policy; the owner's private notes, tasks and contact details remain withheld. Meetings accessible only through domain or anyone-with-link sharing require the note URL and resolve_share_link. Results with shared=true are another person's notes (owner.name): attribute their content and tasks to the people in them, never to the user, unless the user is named as the one who said or committed to it. folders lists the Wispr Flow folders the meeting is filed in that the user can see (their own and ones shared with them), as {id, name} sorted by name; null when it is in none. share_link is the meeting's notes page in Wispr Flow. Give it to the user whenever they ask for a link. Who else can open it depends on that meeting's sharing setting, and this server cannot read or change that setting. If the user wants to change who a link works for, tell them to open the Wispr Flow app, go to the Notetaker tab, click the menu to the right of the meeting, and click Share — that opens the sharing settings for that meeting. A meeting with no share_link has no notes page yet — say so rather than guessing a URL. Every timestamp in the response is UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Convert times to the user's local time zone before presenting them — do not show the raw UTC time to the user.

description.text: Get the recorded meeting — a bounded range of its markdown notes, the complete derived markdown summary, and (when requested and available) a bounded transcript range — captured for a calendar event, by its calendar_id (from search_calendar_events or resolve_calendar_link). Use this to answer 'what was discussed / decided / the action items' for a meeting on the user's calendar. Returns start/end times for when the meeting happened. The raw Lexical notes JSON is intentionally omitted; use paginated `content` and complete `summary`, whose next-steps section holds the meeting's action items. Prefer view_transcript={} and synthesize from the transcript itself: the notes are an auto-generated summary that can drop or distort details, while the transcript is the verbatim source of truth. Omit view_transcript only when you've judged the notes alone are enough. When truncated, use the continuation offset in the marker to request the next range. Content returns its first bounded range by default; use view_content with its continuation offset to read more. If the event exists but no recording is linked to it, returns {recorded: false, reason: 'not_recorded'} with the event's title and times instead of a recording; errors only if the calendar_id is unknown. Available meetings include the user's own meetings, meetings shared with them as an email recipient, and meetings in enabled shared folders they can access. Shared meetings expose the summary and any transcript permitted by sharing policy; the owner's private notes, tasks and contact details remain withheld. Meetings accessible only through domain or anyone-with-link sharing require the note URL and resolve_share_link. Results with shared=true are another person's notes (owner.name): attribute their content and tasks to the people in them, never to the user, unless the user is named as the one who said or committed to it. folders lists the Wispr Flow folders the meeting is filed in that the user can see (their own and ones shared with them), as {id, name} sorted by name; null when it is in none. share_link is the meeting's notes page in Wispr Flow. Give it to the user whenever they ask for a link. Who else can open it depends on that meeting's sharing setting, and this server cannot read or change that setting. If the user wants to change who a link works for, tell them to open the Wispr Flow app, go to the Notetaker tab, click the menu to the right of the meeting, and click Share — that opens the sharing settings for that meeting. A meeting with no share_link has no notes page yet — say so rather than guessing a URL. Every timestamp in the response is UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Convert times to the user's local time zone before presenting them — do not show the raw UTC time to the user.

meeting_id.description: An owned meeting id from search_meetings, without shared:true.

description.text: Who was in a meeting owned by the user and which participant is the user. Shared meeting IDs are unsupported. Returns the user's own name/email/domain plus every participant (speaker-map people and calendar attendees) with name, contact_id, emails, whether they spoke, organizer, role (self | organizer | attendee | speaker-only: in the speaker map but not a calendar attendee), and relationship to the user (self | colleague | external | unknown, by email domain). emails is empty when no address is known. The user's own speaker row, if any, has role self; use the top-level user email for them. Omits the user's calendar row, mention-origin people, and Google room/equipment attendees. Calendar RSVP is not included. When listed, get_participant_contacts takes contact_ids from this result for LinkedIn, job title, and company.

Richer profile for a specific group of meeting participants. Pass contact_ids from get_meeting_participants_enriched (max 50). Returns owner-scoped contacts with display name, email, job title, company, and LinkedIn when enrichment is available. Unknown or non-owned ids are omitted. Only advertised when Wispr Contacts is enabled for the user.

description.text: Get a single upcoming calendar event by calendar_id, with its latest pre-read when one is available. Refuses past events — use get_meeting_by_calendar_id for the recorded notes of a past event, or get_calendar_event for generic event metadata. Pass include_preread=false to skip the pre-read fetch. description.text: List the meeting notes in one folder (id from list_folders or a meeting's `folders` field), newest first, including notes other members filed. `is_mine` marks the user's own notes: read those with get_meeting. Other members' notes carry only a summary; read one with resolve_share_link on its share_link. Results are newest first and paginated: when the response has has_more true, call again with cursor set to its next_cursor (copied verbatim); no next_cursor means the list is complete.

List the Wispr Flow folders the user owns or has been added to, the user's own first. A folder groups related meeting notes (e.g. every 1:1 with a manager); in a shared folder, every member sees the notes filed there. Use when the user names a folder, then call list_folder_meetings with its id. Meeting results also carry a `folders` field, so a meeting's folders are known without calling this.

description.text: Given an owned meeting_id (a search_meetings result without shared:true) for a recurring meeting, list every recorded occurrence of that recurring series — newest first, including the meeting you passed in. Use to answer 'what did we discuss last time this met', 'what's recurred across these syncs', or to catch up before today's instance. If the meeting isn't part of a recurring calendar series, returns {recurring: false, reason: 'not_recurring' | 'no_calendar_event'} with an empty meetings list; errors only if the meeting_id is unknown. Each occurrence has the same shape as a search_meetings result (call get_meeting for full notes/transcript). folders lists the Wispr Flow folders the meeting is filed in that the user can see (their own and ones shared with them), as {id, name} sorted by name; null when it is in none. Results are paginated, newest first. If the response's has_more is true there are more matches: call again with cursor set to the returned next_cursor (copied verbatim) to continue. When more remain, a 'more' field spells out how many and how to continue. To answer 'all'/'every'/'ever' questions, keep paging until has_more is false. Paging is capped at 1000 results per query; truncated=true means more matches exist beyond the cap — narrow the query. Every timestamp in the response is UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Convert times to the user's local time zone before presenting them — do not show the raw UTC time to the user.

description.text: Get the transcript, notes, or summary of a Wispr Flow meeting from a share link (https://notes.wisprflow.ai/shared/… or its bare slug). Use this rather than fetching the page, which does not include the transcript. Returns the title, Flow Summary (whose next-steps section holds the meeting's action items), owner, and the caller's role. The owner also receives their user-authored My Notes. Pass view_transcript={} when the user wants the transcript: a bounded range is returned only when the caller owns the note or is an explicitly invited recipient AND the owner's organization shares transcripts. Domain/team access, anyone-with-link access, or a notes-only organization returns transcript=null plus a transcript_access explanation when requested. When truncated, use the continuation offset in the marker to request the next range. Errors if the link is not a share link or no shared note is accessible for it. Every timestamp in the response is UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Convert times to the user's local time zone before presenting them — do not show the raw UTC time to the user.

attendee_match.description: How to combine multiple attendee_emails: 'any' (default) matches anyone in the list; 'all' matches only items where every listed attendee was present. Ignored for a single email.

until.description: Only events starting strictly before this ISO datetime with offset/Z. Use the next local midnight for a day filter.

description.text: Search or list the user's Google Calendar events. Use to find meetings by who's on them (attendee_emails — the precise way to answer 'meetings with alex@acme.com', or 'with both alex and bob' via attendee_match=all), by keyword in the title/description, or within a date window. For a whole local calendar day (including earlier events), use since and until. Returns each event's title, time, conference URL, and an attendee preview (up to 5 structured attendees plus attendee_count). Use get_calendar_event for the complete attendee list. Note: these are calendar events, not the recorded meeting notes. Results are paginated, newest first. If the response's has_more is true there are more matches: call again with cursor set to the returned next_cursor (copied verbatim) to continue. When more remain, a 'more' field spells out how many and how to continue. To answer 'all'/'every'/'ever' questions, keep paging until has_more is false. description.text: Search or list meetings captured by Wispr Flow Meeting Recorder. Use when the user asks about their meetings, calls, standups, 1:1s, syncs, or anything discussed in a recorded conversation. Returns the most recently modified meetings when no query is given. For meetings on a particular day, pass since/until (when the meeting happened, half-open). Filter by who was there with attendee_emails (matched against the meeting's linked calendar event) — the precise way to answer 'my meetings with alex@acme.com'. Each result lists up to 5 attendees (more are summarized — call get_meeting for the full list), start/end times, and a has_transcript flag; when true, follow up with get_meeting and view_transcript={} and answer from the transcript rather than the lossy notes summary. Available meetings include the user's own meetings, meetings shared with them as an email recipient, and meetings in enabled shared folders they can access. Shared meetings expose the summary and any transcript permitted by sharing policy; the owner's private notes, tasks and contact details remain withheld. Meetings accessible only through domain or anyone-with-link sharing require the note URL and resolve_share_link. Results with shared=true are another person's notes (owner.name): attribute their content and tasks to the people in them, never to the user, unless the user is named as the one who said or committed to it. folders lists the Wispr Flow folders the meeting is filed in that the user can see (their own and ones shared with them), as {id, name} sorted by name; null when it is in none. share_link is the meeting's notes page in Wispr Flow. Give it to the user whenever they ask for a link. Who else can open it depends on that meeting's sharing setting, and this server cannot read or change that setting. If the user wants to change who a link works for, tell them to open the Wispr Flow app, go to the Notetaker tab, click the menu to the right of the meeting, and click Share — that opens the sharing settings for that meeting. A meeting with no share_link has no notes page yet — say so rather than guessing a URL. Results are paginated, newest first. If the response's has_more is true there are more matches: call again with cursor set to the returned next_cursor (copied verbatim) to continue. When more remain, a 'more' field says how many, exactly up to 100 and as '100+' beyond that, and how to continue. To answer 'all'/'every'/'ever' questions, keep paging until has_more is false. Paging is capped at 1000 results per query; truncated=true means more matches exist beyond the cap — narrow the query. Every timestamp in the response is UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Convert times to the user's local time zone before presenting them — do not show the raw UTC time to the user.
